ai.title: Preload agent info before @ menu
ai.summary: Preload `getLocalAgentInfo()` before `setTimeout` in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. Await promise inside timeout callback to prevent race conditions when displaying agent menu.

eli5.text: When you type the '@' symbol in the command-line tool, a menu of available assistants now appears more reliably without showing outdated or empty information. The tool now gathers the list of available assistants before pausing briefly to check if you're pasting multiple lines of text, so the menu always reflects the current state. This prevents a timing issue where the menu could open before the assistant data was ready.

ai.title: Publish multiple agents at once
ai.summary: CLI publish command now accepts multiple agent IDs. Shared Zod schemas in common/src/types/api/agents/publish.ts define batch request/response payloads. Web API route and CLI handler updated to process arrays of DynamicAgentTemplate. Error responses include availablePublishers and validationErrors for each agent in the batch.

eli5.text: You can now publish several agents at the same time instead of one by one. When you run the publish command in the terminal or send a request to the website's API, you can give it a list of agent IDs and it will upload all of them together, reporting success or failure for each one. If some fail, you get a clear list showing which ones had problems and what went wrong with each, plus any available publishers you could choose from.

ai.title: publisher field required for agent publishing
ai.summary: Publishing agents now requires a `publisher` field in the agent config. The `--publisher` CLI flag and `publisherId` API parameter are removed. The publish route validates that all agents in a request share the same publisher ID.

eli5.text: When you publish an agent now, you must declare who is publishing it directly inside the agent's own config file, using a new "publisher" entry. The separate command-line flag and the web publishing form no longer ask for or accept a publisher ID; instead, the publishing endpoint checks that every agent you try to publish in one go lists the same publisher, and rejects the request if they do not match. If you have been publishing agents, you will need to add your publisher ID to each agent's config before you can publish, and you can only publish agents that share the same publisher in a single batch.

ai.title: Remove parent instructions validation from agent template validation
ai.summary: Removed `validateParentInstructions` and `formatParentInstructionsError` calls from `validateSingleAgent` in `common/src/templates/agent-validation.ts`. The validation block checking `template.parentInstructions` against `dynamicAgentIds` is deleted. Imports for these functions are also removed. This fixes a typecheck error.

eli5.text: The agent-builder now skips checking that every listed parent instruction refers to an existing agent, so templates with unknown parent entries are accepted instead of producing a type-check error. If you author an agent template with parent instructions, you'll no longer get blocked at validation time for referencing agents by identifiers that the builder can’t confirm exist. This is live with the latest release.

ai.title: Add typecheck for tool call strings
ai.summary: getToolCallString now enforces strict Zod types for parameters when the tool name is a known ToolName, rejecting invalid keys or shapes at compile time. Example prompts in base-prompts.ts and prompts.ts were updated to use str_replace instead of write_file to match current tool schemas. send-agent-message, spawn-agents, and spawn-agents-async examples now pass native objects instead of JSON.stringify'd strings to params. This change affects backend tool definitions and common utilities, improving developer experience by catching tool usage errors before runtime.

eli5.text: Now, when an example shows how to ask me to find and edit part of a file, it tells you the exact old text and new text to replace instead of asking me to rewrite the whole file, so you get safer, more reliable edits. If you write one of these examples yourself, my tools will reject typos like a misspelled parameter name or a value shaped the wrong way before I ever try to run it, pointing the problem back to you immediately. The built-in examples bundled inside This is live today.

ai.title: Add Windows multiline git commit prompt guidance
ai.summary: Updated system prompt in `backend/src/system-prompt/prompts.ts` to include specific instructions for multiline git commits on Windows. The prompt now advises ending each line with `^` to ensure correct parsing of the commit message body. This change addresses potential shell interpretation issues on Windows environments.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to create a git commit on a Windows computer, it now includes special instructions telling you to add a caret (^) at the end of each line of the commit message. This prevents Windows' command line from misreading multiline commit messages. If you're on Windows and look at the commit instructions, you'll see these new step-by-step directions that don't appear for users on other operating systems.

ai.title: Update strreplace tool example to show tab indentation
ai.summary: The str_replace tool definition example in backend/src/tools/definitions/tool/str-replace.ts now includes a replacement case with tab characters. This demonstrates proper handling of indented code blocks during string replacement. The change affects only the tool's documentation example, not its functional logic.

eli5.text: The written guide showing people how to use the search-and-replace feature now includes an example that uses tab characters for indentation. Before, the guide only showed simple one-line replacements, so readers couldn't see how properly indented code blocks would work. Now, when someone reads the instructions, they will see an example that demonstrates handling lines containing tabs and spacing, making the instructions match how code typically appears in real files. This change only affects the instructional example text itself, not the actual search-and-replace functionality.

ai.title: Update eval superagent instructions
ai.summary: Enhanced `run-git-evals.ts` to render detailed agent steps including tool calls and results, replacing simple response text. Added explicit instruction to the superagent judge that file changes require tool calls, preventing false positives for completion. This improves the accuracy of automated eval judgments by providing richer context and clearer constraints.

eli5.text: When the system automatically reviews whether an agent successfully completed a coding task, it now shows the full step-by-step reasoning instead of just the final answer. This means you get a clearer picture of what the agent did, including which tools it used and the results those tools returned. Additionally, the automatic reviewer now explicitly checks that actual file edits were made through tool calls, preventing situations where it might incorrectly judge a task as finished when no real changes occurred.

ai.title: Evals CI concurrency raised to 100
ai.summary: The `run-eval-set` command in `.github/workflows/evals.yml` now uses `--concurrency 100` instead of 10. This change aims to speed up the evaluation process by increasing the number of parallel evaluations. Scope is limited to the CI workflow configuration.

eli5.text: The system now runs 10 times as many evaluation tests at once, so the background checks that make sure new versions work correctly finish faster. This only affects internal testing processes, not what you see when using the product. Nothing about your access, experience, or the live service changes because of this.

ai.title: Git evals continue without prompt
ai.summary: run-git-evals.ts no longer throws when agent decides 'continue' with missing next_prompt. Sets next_prompt to 'continue' string instead. Affects evals/git-evals/run-git-evals.ts. Prevents eval crashes on superagent prompt omission.

eli5.text: When the assistant running an automated evaluation decided to keep going but forgot to suggest what to try next, the system used to crash and stop the whole evaluation. Now, instead of stopping, it simply fills in a default next step and lets the evaluation continue. This only affects the internal automated testing tool that checks how the assistant behaves; if you're not running those tests, you wouldn't see any difference.

ai.title: evals.yml concurrency reduced to 10
ai.summary: Eval workflow concurrency limit reduced from 100 to 10. Change applied to .github/workflows/evals.yml run-eval-set command. Mitigates resource contention or rate limits during evaluation runs.

eli5.text: The system that runs quality checks on new features now runs those checks more cautiously, spacing out how many happen at the same time. Previously, it would run up to 100 checks simultaneously, which could overwhelm shared resources or hit usage limits. Now it caps the parallel checks at 10. This change is live today and affects only internal testing processes; you wouldn't notice it directly, but your team will see smoother, more reliable automated evaluations when new code is submitted.

ai.title: Remove cbeasp from agent builder templates
ai.summary: Removed cb_easp: false flags from agent builder template definitions in base-agent-builder.ts. Deleted unused AGENT_PERSONAS import. Internal cleanup of agent template configuration.

eli5.text: When the system sets up a new agent assistant for you, it used to attach an extra on/off switch to each step of the setup process that wasn't needed. Those switches have been pulled off, so the setup steps are now fewer lines of instructions. If you watched a new agent being created, you'd see the same files and actions happen, just without those unnecessary flags cluttering each step. Who is affected: people who build or use custom agent assistants through the system. The change is in place today.

ai.title: baselite agent model set to openrouter/horizon-beta
ai.summary: base_lite template model updated from gemini2_5_flash to openrouter/horizon-beta in backend/src/templates/agent-list.ts. Import order for baseAgentBuilder adjusted. Internal config change for lite mode agent.

eli5.text: The lighter-weight version of the assistant now uses a different AI model behind the scenes to generate its responses. If you use the lite mode of the assistant, you can keep using it exactly as before - nothing about how you interact with it changes, it's just talking to a different engine internally that the team decided works better for this simplified mode. This change only affects the internal configuration and doesn't alter any features or behavior you see.
